# stalwart_directory_oidc (Data Source)

Defines an external directory for account authentication and lookups. Reads the OpenID Connect variant.



<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `id` (String) Identifier of the object.

### Read-Only

- `accepted_audiences` (Set of String) Additional values accepted in the token's aud claim besides this server's resource identifiers. Use it for the audience the identity provider puts in access tokens, for example the client id of the web interface, an API identifier, or a project id.
- `allow_id_token_claims` (Boolean) Accept JWT access tokens that carry ID token claims such as nonce or at_hash. Needed for providers whose access tokens are copies of the ID token. When enabled, an ID token can be presented as an access token.
- `allow_invalid_certs` (Boolean) Allow invalid TLS certificates when connecting to the OpenID Connect provider
- `claim_groups` (String) The claim name used to retrieve the user's group memberships from the token or user info response. Common values are groups or roles depending on the provider's configuration. If not set, group information will not be populated. Note that some providers omit group claims from the token to keep its size small and only return them via the user info endpoint. When it is set and the access token does not carry the claim, every login calls the user info endpoint to fetch it.
- `claim_name` (String) The claim name used to retrieve the user's display name from the token or user info response. Common values are name or display_name. If not set, the display name will not be populated. When it is set and the access token does not carry the claim, every login calls the provider's user info endpoint to fetch it, so leave it unset unless the provider includes it in access tokens or the extra request is acceptable.
- `claim_username` (String) The claim name used to retrieve the user's login name from the token or user info response. Common values are preferred_username, email, or sub depending on the provider's configuration. If the claim value is not an email address and usernameDomain is set, the domain will be appended automatically (e.g. john becomes john@example.com). If the claim value already contains an @, it is used as-is. If the claim value is not an email address and no usernameDomain is configured, Stalwart will fall back to the email claim. If neither yields a valid email address, authentication will be rejected.
- `description` (String) Short description of this directory
- `introspection_auth_method` (String) How the server authenticates to the introspection endpoint
- `introspection_client_id` (String) Client id used to authenticate to the introspection endpoint
- `introspection_client_secret` (Attributes) Client secret used to authenticate to the introspection endpoint (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--introspection_client_secret))
- `issuer_url` (String) The issuer URL of the OpenID Connect provider (e.g. https://sso.example.com/realms/myrealm). It is compared exactly with the issuer reported by the provider, so enter it exactly as the provider reports it, including any trailing slash. Endpoints are discovered from /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server first and then from /.well-known/openid-configuration. For Microsoft Entra ID, use the tenant-specific issuer.
- `lenient_issuer_match` (Boolean) Ignore a trailing slash difference between the configured issuer URL and the issuer reported by the provider and found in tokens
- `member_tenant_id` (String) Identifier for the tenant this directory belongs to Requires an Enterprise license.
- `opaque_token_validation` (String) How access tokens that are not JWTs are validated. Disabled rejects them. User info calls the provider's UserInfo endpoint, which cannot check the token's audience or scopes, so any token the provider issued to any application is accepted, with the access set by the tokens without scopes option. Introspection calls the provider's RFC 7662 introspection endpoint, checks audience and scopes, and requires client credentials. Only one method is used per token.
- `skip_audience_validation` (Boolean) Accept access tokens whose aud claim is missing or matches none of this server's resource identifiers or accepted audiences. Tokens issued to any application at the provider will then be accepted.
- `trusted_provider` (Boolean) Let a directory owned by a tenant contact its provider on private networks and over plain HTTP, as a directory owned by the server does. Only a superuser can save a directory with this setting enabled, so a tenant administrator cannot change a trusted directory afterwards. Requires an Enterprise license.
- `unscoped_tokens` (String) How access tokens that carry none of the interoperable mail, contacts, calendars or files scopes are handled. Tokens issued to this server's web interface always have full access. Reject follows the OAuth profile for open public clients. Interoperable services grants access to mail, contacts, calendars and files, which is enough for mail clients when the provider cannot issue these scopes. Full access also grants management permissions to any such token and should only be used together with a strict audience check.
- `username_domain` (String) The domain name to append to the username when the value of claimUsername does not contain an @ symbol (e.g. setting this to example.com will turn john into john@example.com). If not set, Stalwart will fall back to the email claim when the username claim does not contain a valid email address.
